object_wins.rule: For each of the 17 keys of results{}, compared results[obj]['GRUctx|lag3']['seg_f1'] > results[obj]['SF|lag3']['seg_f1'] with strict >; one object = one vote, no rows or episodes involved. (Same comparison on inputs/CRPS_L2_ALGO_ROUND.json gives only 15/17.)

episode_claim.why: Deduplicating the 1464 object-episode rows of results[obj]['episode_paired'] down to the 111 unique episodes and taking each episode's mean dSegF1 gives 97 positive / 14 negative from CRPS_L2_EVAL.json and 92/19 from CRPS_L2_ALGO_ROUND.json. No 96 appears in either pairing; the audit's own date_signs sum to 96 only because it records 26/34 for 2025-01-13 where the EVAL pairing yields 27/34.

strongest_deployable_baseline.scheme: SF|lag3 (single-frame logistic regression, no context, lag 3)
strongest_deployable_baseline.why_the_others_are_not_eligible: SFA_Oracle|lag3 (0.8236) is an oracle upper bound requiring the true parent action every frame, Shufctx|lag3 (0.4098) and GateCtx|lag3 (0.7093) are a shuffled control and a tuned variant of the champion rather than deployable competitors, and GRUskill|lag3 (0.6514) / DualHead|lag3 (0.6468) are LODO-eligible but already fall below SF, so SF is the strongest legal-input baseline that the champion must beat.

does_not_license: These DEV-only, 17-correlated-fold numbers do not license any 'unseen-object' or state-of-the-art claim, nor the 96/111 coverage figure: the folds share ~76 of ~86 test episodes and 14.5 training episodes per pair, the gain is label-level while boundary F1 is flat, and the sealed 37 recordings were never evaluated.
method:
1) Loaded the four input JSONs read-only and enumerated the actual key paths instead of trusting the report; no network, no re-training (only per-object metric dicts and per-episode pairings exist, no predictions or frames).
2) object_macro_segF1 = unweighted mean over the 17 entries of results[obj][scheme]['seg_f1'] for scheme in {'SF|lag3','GRUctx|lag3'}: EVAL 0.671750 / 0.713501; ALGO_ROUND 0.671750 / 0.709091.
3) object_wins = count of objects with GRUctx seg_f1 strictly greater than SF seg_f1: 17/17 in EVAL, 15/17 in ALGO_ROUND.
4) Episode claim: pooled all results[obj]['episode_paired'] rows (1464 rows, 111 unique episode ids), averaged dSegF1 per episode id, counted signs: EVAL 97/111 (mean d = +0.0446), ALGO_ROUND 92/111; per-date recount matches the audit's date_signs except 2025-01-13 (27 vs declared 26).
5) Cross-checks: GateCtx beats GRUctx on 8/17 objects and on 20/111 episodes (the report's '1.6%' is 23/1464 object-episode rows = 1.57%), boundary F1_full_0.5 macro 0.5948 (SF) vs 0.5894 (GRUctx), and Paired Wilcoxon on the 111 EVAL episode deltas gives W=508, p=2.0e-14 (audit declares W=493, p=1.4e-14).
